title.quote: Implicit Diffusion: Efficient optimization through stochastic sampling
title.justification: The title appears at the head of the paper.
title.value: Implicit Diffusion: Efficient optimization through stochastic sampling

extractions.description: Introduces and evaluates Implicit Diffusion, a single-loop procedure that jointly performs stochastic sampling and parameter optimization, with experiments on Langevin energy-based models and reward finetuning of denoising diffusion models.

type.quote: We provide theoretical and experimental results showcasing the performance of our method.
type.justification: The paper includes both theory and executed experiments; its empirical runs make it an empirical study for this catalogue.

name.quote: Sampling from a target distribution is a ubiquitous task at the heart of various methods in machine learning, optimization, and statistics.
name.justification: The paper explicitly situates its contribution in machine learning.

name.quote: we introduce Implicit Diffusion optimization, a single-loop optimization algorithm to optimize through sampling.
name.justification: Optimization through stochastic sampling is the central field advanced by the new algorithm.

name.quote: This allows us to draw a link between optimization through stochastic sampling and bilevel optimization
name.justification: The method advances a distribution-valued analogue of bilevel optimization.

name.quote: This approach is inspired by recent advances in bilevel optimization and automatic implicit differentiation
name.justification: Automatic implicit differentiation is a methodological field directly addressed by the framework.

name.quote: Applications include finetuning denoising diffusions and training energy-based models.
name.justification: Denoising diffusion model finetuning is an experimental application domain advanced by the paper.

name.quote: Applications include finetuning denoising diffusions and training energy-based models.
name.justification: Energy-based model training is another experimental application domain.

is_contributed.quote: Applications include finetuning denoising diffusions and training energy-based models.
is_contributed.justification: The energy-based model class is an application of the contributed algorithm, not itself introduced as a new model architecture.

is_executed.quote: We use Implicit Diffusion where the reward is the KL between the target distribution and the current one. We train for K = 40, 000 steps with a batch of size 1, 000.
is_executed.justification: The paper trained energy-based Gaussian-mixture models.

is_compared.quote: Evolution of the reward and of the log-likelihood of the samples for the initial model, for the Implicit Diffusion algorithm, and for the trained model after Implicit Diffusion.
is_compared.justification: The initial and trained energy-based models are numerically compared through reward and log-likelihood curves.

name.quote: We report results on models pretrained on the image datasets MNIST (LeCun and Cortes, 1998), CIFAR-10 (Krizhevsky, 2009), and LSUN (bedrooms) (Yu et al., 2016).

is_contributed.quote: For pretraining, we follow the simple diffusion method (Hoogeboom et al., 2023) and use U-Net models (Ronneberger et al., 2015).
is_contributed.justification: The architecture and diffusion-model family are existing assets; the contribution is the optimization procedure.

is_executed.quote: We also apply Implicit Diffusion for reward finetuning of denoising diffusion models pretrained on image datasets.
is_executed.justification: The models are pretrained, finetuned, and sampled in this paper.

is_compared.quote: We report selected samples of π ⋆ (θt ), as well as reward and KL divergence estimates
is_compared.justification: Different finetuning configurations are evaluated numerically, but there is no numerical comparison against a distinct model family; therefore this is not treated as a model-to-model comparison.
